**Written Statement Regarding October 27 Afternoon Transportation**  
**To:** Mrs. Okafor  
**Copy:** Darlene, Transportation Supervisor; Transportation Office  
**From:** [Your Name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary  
**Date:** [Date Submitted]  
**Re:** Amara Okafor, Fairmont Elementary — Complaint dated October 29

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am submitting this statement in response to your October 29 complaint regarding Amara’s afternoon bus ride on Tuesday, October 27. My supervisor, Darlene, provided the complaint to me on November 3 and requested my written response by November 13. I want to explain what happened, address your concerns respectfully, and make sure the record accurately reflects why I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary.

I understand that not finding your child where you expected her to be would be frightening. I have grandchildren, and I can appreciate how upsetting that uncertainty must have been. I am sorry for the worry you experienced that afternoon. My decision to keep Amara on the bus and return her to school was made for her safety and in accordance with the district’s kindergarten dismissal rule.

On October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara’s stop was at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. The scheduled arrival time was 3:50 p.m., and I arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m. Amara has a green tag on her bag identifying her as a student who must have an adult present at the stop before she can be released.

I remained at the stop until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I did not see an adult waiting for Amara at the corner. Under the district rule for kindergarten riders, when no adult is present to receive the child, the student stays on the bus and is returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. Because I could not see an adult there to receive Amara, I did not allow her to leave the bus.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch to report the situation. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. At that point, I still had three stops to complete and 14 children remaining on the bus. I continued the route with Amara safely aboard and then returned her to Fairmont Elementary.

We arrived at Fairmont at approximately 4:31 p.m. I personally walked Amara into the school and handed her over to Mrs. Petrakis in the office. I did not leave her outside the building or send her into the school alone.

I understand from your complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved to me. I did not see you or your wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, which may have affected visibility. I cannot say exactly what you could see from your position, but I can state clearly that I did not knowingly ignore you or refuse to acknowledge you. If I had seen you, I would have been able to address your presence before leaving the stop.

While responsible for the children aboard the bus, I could not leave them unattended to walk across the road or search for an adult whose location I did not know. My responsibility was to supervise the students, make a safe decision about Amara’s release, and follow the district’s procedure when I could not identify an adult at the stop.

I also want to address the statement that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing as I left the stop. I was directing a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down while we were pulling out. I understand that something seen from outside the bus may have been interpreted differently, but I was attending to a student’s behavior and the safe operation of the bus, not making light of you or the situation.

During the remainder of the ride, Amara appeared comfortable. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her that we were going on a little extra trip. I kept my explanation calm and simple for her age. Her appearing comfortable does not lessen the concern you felt, but I include this information so that you know what I observed while she was in my care.

I respectfully request that the Transportation Office promptly retrieve, preserve, and review the available bus camera footage from that afternoon, including any available audio. The review should include our arrival and wait at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, our departure from the stop, and the return to Fairmont Elementary. That footage may help clarify visibility at the stop, my interaction with the student in seat 2, and the events described in this statement. I ask that it be considered along with the complaint and my response.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years without a write-up. I take that responsibility seriously, particularly when transporting young children who depend on adults to make safe decisions for them. I include my work history as part of the record, but I also recognize that your concern deserves a clear response based on what happened that afternoon.

To help prevent another misunderstanding, I ask that, consistent with the school’s directions for the stop, you wait where you are clearly visible to me on the bus side of the street. If you arrive by car, please step out and make yourself visible from a safe location rather than relying on a wave from inside or beside a parked vehicle across the street. I would welcome the Transportation Office’s help in confirming a safe, clear pickup arrangement that works for everyone.

I am glad to continue driving Amara and want her daily ride to remain comfortable and positive. I also want you to feel confident that her safety is my priority. On October 27, I followed the district’s procedure because I did not see an adult available to receive her. I hope this explanation and a review of the camera footage will help resolve your concerns and allow us to move forward respectfully.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]  
School Bus Driver  
Bus 41 — Route 9 Elementary
